verdicts.note: Attacked on magnitude and applicability: she concedes the assessor does not set tax policy [S5], so this is an advocacy goal rather than a power of the office. But the direction is explicit and repeated: join the assessors' exemption committee and push for a state homestead exemption [S2][S5], 'make our property taxes more affordable' [S3], 'ever-increasing property taxes' [S5]. That is pole_a's 'reduce the tax burden' through a targeted exemption. She opposes no specific new tax, so -1 rather than -2. Three sources: medium holds.

Attacked on magnitude: she has more than eight years as a Skamania County employee and 20 as a paralegal [S1][S5], so she is not a pure outsider. But she has never held office, this is her first run [S7], and her pitch is explicitly 'change' and 'a fresh perspective' against a two-decade incumbent [S2][S5]. The axis describes profile, and her profile and pitch are renewal: +2 medium holds. Citation nit: the basis quotes the slogan 'It's Time for a Change', which does not appear verbatim in the dossier (it records 'change' and 'fresh perspective' [S2][S5]). Paraphrase it or drop the quotation marks.

Attacked on direction: a business personal property exemption is relief for a narrow class, and his record is administration, not tax policy. But it is a tax-burden reduction he has worked for through the assessors' association ($3,000 to $15,000, now seeking $50,000 'or potentially even higher') [S2], and he takes no position for new revenue. Single source, so -1 medium (not higher) is right.

Assessor since 2002 by his account [S2], re-elected unopposed in 2022 [S5], and his pamphlet statement asks to 'continue this important work' with his staff [S1]. Textbook pole_a; the narrow primary loss [S4] does not change the profile. -2 high holds.

note: Missing scores considered and not proposed: spending for Moser (her opposition to selling the fairgrounds parking lot [S2] is a land-use dispute, not audit-vs-invest; the DOR audit she posts [S6] concerns his office's procedure), housing for Moser (she says housing is the county's greater need [S2] but states no market-vs-public remedy), and reform for both (nothing on political money; Moser's PDC mini-reporter status [S8] is not a reform position). Display review: office_does matches contest S1 and S5. race_blurb is accurate and neutral except for one word: it calls Moser a 'former paralegal', but the dossier records only '20 years of paralegal experience' plus county employment [S1][S5], and _contest.md calls her 'a county employee and paralegal'. Suggest 'a county employee with 20 years as a paralegal'. Moser's summary and all five highlights match S1, S2, S4, S5 and S7. Spencer's summary ('in the office since 2002' is his own dating [S2]) and four highlights match S2, S3 and S4. The DOR audit highlight is stated neutrally.
